title: Vertical Farming
desc: Plan and run a small indoor or stacked farm: crops, light, water, nutrients, climate, food safety and business case.
outcomes: Explain how stacked growing works and what suits it.
Set light, water and nutrient schedules.
Compute yield, energy and water per kilogram.
task: Plan and run a small stacked growing pilot with schedules, logs, hygiene plan, harvest records and unit economics.
condition: A small space or shelving kit, lights, seeds, a spreadsheet, two peers and a grower mentor.
standard: Schedules are followed and logged; yield per tray recorded; hygiene plan applied; energy and water per kg calculated; cost per kg shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Growers, hospitality staff, school teachers, urban entrepreneurs.
evidence: plan, daily log, harvest record, cost sheet
modules: High-value, fast, light crops: lettuce, herbs, microgreens.
Water flows with nutrients; no soil.
A timer controls a flood and drain tray.
Keep water clean; change on schedule.
Clean tools, hands and trays; keep pests out.
Mould appears at high humidity; fans fix it.
kWh per kg and litres per kg.
3.5 kg per tray; 9 kWh per kg.
Setup cost, running cost, price per kg.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: water management, alternative protein, greenhouse gas auditing.
local: Food safety and water rules differ by place.
ladder: What suits vertical growing

L1: learner can name crops. Focus module: What suits vertical growing (Understand, 3 h). Leafy and herbs first. Key points: High-value, fast, light crops: lettuce, herbs, microgreens. Heavy crops are harder. Weigh space, energy and market.

Teach: open with the worked example. Microgreens ready in 8 days. Then set the activity: Pick three crops. Mark against the standard: Reasons given. Check at this level: Which crops suit? Model answer: Leafy greens, herbs, microgreens. Crops.
Systems

L2: learner knows system types. Focus module: Systems (Understand, 4 h). Soil, hydroponic, aeroponic. Key points: Water flows with nutrients; no soil. Pumps, trays, channels. Failure risk if pumps stop.

Teach: open with the worked example. A timer controls a flood and drain tray. Then set the activity: Draw a layout. Mark against the standard: Parts labelled. Check at this level: Why LEDs? Model answer: Efficient, less heat. Systems.
Light
L3: learner can set schedules. Focus module: Light (Apply, 4 h). Plants need the right light. Key points: Intensity, spectrum and hours. LEDs use less heat. Distance matters.

Teach: open with the worked example. Lettuce gets 14 hours a day. Then set the activity: Set a light schedule. Mark against the standard: Settings logged. Check at this level: What pH range? Model answer: About 5.8 to 6.2 for many crops. Light.
Water and nutrients
L4: learner can run a tray. Focus module: Water and nutrients (Apply, 4 h). Balance matters. Key points: pH and nutrient strength checks. Keep water clean; change on schedule. Record readings.

Teach: open with the worked example. pH kept between 5.8 and 6.2. Then set the activity: Run daily checks. Mark against the standard: Log complete. Check at this level: Why hygiene? Model answer: Prevent disease. Run.
Climate and hygiene

L5: learner can measure yield. Focus module: Climate and hygiene (Evaluate, 4 h). Prevent disease. Key points: Temperature, humidity and airflow. Clean tools, hands and trays; keep pests out. Separate harvest area.

Teach: open with the worked example. Mould appears at high humidity; fans fix it. Then set the activity: Write a hygiene plan. Mark against the standard: Measures specific. Check at this level: Yield measure? Model answer: Per m2 per cycle. Maths.
Business case
L6: learner can lead a farm shift. Focus module: Business case (Evaluate, 4 h). Does it pay? Key points: Setup cost, running cost, price per kg. Direct sales and contracts. Break-even volume.

Teach: open with the worked example. Price 250 INR per kg; cost 190. Then set the activity: Build a cost sheet. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Energy per kg unit? Model answer: kWh per kg. Lead.
Pilot plan
L7: learner can audit a plan. Focus module: Pilot plan (Create, 3 h). Run 90 days. Key points: Targets and weekly reviews. Learn from losses. Decide to scale or stop.

Teach: open with the worked example. Pilot gives 62 kg of herbs. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Mark against the standard: Peers follow it. Check at this level: Biggest risk? Model answer: Pump or power failure. Peer audit.
